name: Peltier (thermoelectric) modules
summary: Flat ceramic squares that pump heat from one face to the other on DC, or make a little power from a temperature difference.
uses: Small cooler for medicine or drinks (power-hungry: about 50W for a small box)
Condensing water out of damp air
A few watts from a stove-top generator
identify: Thin white squares about 40 × 40 mm with a red and a black wire, often marked TEC1-12706 (12V, about 6A). Found in car and drinks coolers, small cosmetic or wine fridges and some dehumidifiers, always sandwiched between heatsinks and fans.
test: Touch the wires to a 1.5–5V battery: one face should go cold and the other warm within seconds. Never run one at 12V without a heatsink: the hot side burns you and the module dies in seconds.

decay.note: Lasts if kept dry; damp can get past the edge seal.
